summary: A one-to-one coaching session between closer Richard Claessen and sales coach Chris Klevan, built around a recorded call review. Richard opens with his pipeline state — a disqualified lead, a reschedule, two new bookings — and says his weakness is objection handling with high achievers who have no urgency. Chris then plays back a recording of Richard's pitch and coaches him to cut the length of the presentation dramatically, to stop answering 'does that make sense?' as the only buy-in, to withhold deliverables until the prospect asks, and to stop getting defensive when a payment question arrives. The session closes on detachment work — making it okay to miss a close, miss projections, or be fired — and a scripted trust-objection rebuttal.
notable: Chris coaches a specific handling for a direct payment-options question: say 'most guys paid all up front' and then stop talking, and if pressed with 'you don't have any other solutions?' respond 'why do you ask?' rather than disclose that plans exist.
Chris identifies that Richard dropped straight to a trial on a $6,000 offer on the reviewed call: 'And you immediately dropped to a trial with this guy.'
Richard states the Fathom recorder intermittently fails, meaning some calls are never captured: 'my Fathom sometimes really isn't working'.
Richard manages to a closing-rate target: 'If I want to keep my closing rate at the same rate, then at least one should come in.'
Approximately 240 leads belonging to a departed rep, Michael, were redistributed between Richard and Andrew — Richard received about 120.
Chris supplies a scripted proof claim for the trust objection: Trevor has 1.4 million Instagram followers and has 'helped over 1,200 people... We've proven it 1,200 times'.

Chris coaches the consequence frame as an explicit invitation to walk away — 'you genuinely don't have to do anything. You have a great life' — and frames it as leading with truth rather than manipulation.
Detachment coaching used performance-loss framing: 'You need to make it okay to miss projections. You need to make it okay to be fired.'
